chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'There is no thing except that I have assigned to it one who takes possession of it other than Me, except for charity (sadaqah), for I receive it with My Hand with a reception, to the extent that a man gives charity with a single date or half a date, so I nurture it for him just as a man nurtures his foal and his young camel, so it comes on the Day of Resurrection and it is like Mount Uhud and greater than Mount Uhud.'

key_terms.أُحُد: Mount Uhud (used as a measure of size)

ai.seo_question: How does Allah reward small charity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this Hadith Qudsi highlights Allah’s personal involvement in rewarding charity, distinguishing it from other divine decrees managed by angels. The metaphor of nurturing a single date like a young camel underscores the exponential multiplication of rewards for even minimal sincere giving, a concept deeply rooted in the theological emphasis on the merit of small, consistent acts of worship.
